name: Use of English
topics: Conditional sentences, reported speech and active/passive voice

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
After weeks of intense heat, the farmers were happy to see the COPIOUS rainfall.
questions.e: The word 'copious' means abundant in supply or quantity. In this context, the farmers were happy because there was a large amount of rainfall after a dry spell.
questions.p: 'Copious' mean say something plenty well-well. Since hot weather don pay them before, the farmers happy say heavy rain fall.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The principal's speech was so VERBOSE that many students started sleeping.
questions.e: The word 'verbose' means using more words than are needed. This explains why the speech was boring and made the students fall asleep.
questions.p: 'Verbose' mean say person dey use too many words talk. The principal use too much words na why the students begin sleep.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
Chinedu's claim that he met the governor yesterday is SPURIOUS.
questions.e: The word 'spurious' means not being what it purports to be, false, or fake. Therefore, Chinedu's claim is untrue.
questions.p: 'Spurious' mean say something no be true or na fake. So, the thing wey Chinedu talk say he see governor na lie.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The new government policy received TEPID support from the civil servants.
questions.e: The word 'tepid' literally means lukewarm. Figuratively, it means showing little enthusiasm or half-hearted support.
questions.p: 'Tepid' mean say something just dey warm-warm, e no hot. So, the civil servants no really show major ginger for the new policy.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
Under the harsh economic conditions, the value of the local currency began to PLUMMET.
questions.e: To 'plummet' means to fall or drop straight down at a high speed. In an economic crisis, a currency's value plunges or drops drastically.
questions.p: 'Plummet' mean to fall down sharply and fast-fast. As economy bad, the money value just drop kpa.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The accused politician tried to MITIGATE his offense by returning the stolen funds.
questions.e: To 'mitigate' means to make something less severe, serious, or painful. By returning the money, the politician tried to lessen the gravity of his crime.
questions.p: 'Mitigate' mean to reduce or make pain or punishment light. The politician return money to make the matter small.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The class prefect was commended for his EXEMPLARY behavior during the inter-house sports.
questions.e: 'Exemplary' means serving as a desirable model, representing the best of its kind, and therefore commendable or worthy of imitation.
questions.p: 'Exemplary' mean say character good well-well, e dey worthy of praise and make others copy am.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
Halima is an INDEFATIGABLE campaigner for girl-child education in northern Nigeria.
questions.e: The word 'indefatigable' describes someone who persists tirelessly and does not give up easily.
questions.p: 'Indefatigable' mean person wey no dey tire to do something. Halima dey pursue girl-child education without giving up at all.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The judge found the witness's statement to be INCONGRUOUS with the evidence presented.
questions.e: 'Incongruous' means out of keeping or not in harmony with. This means the witness's statement was incompatible or did not match the evidence.
questions.p: 'Incongruous' mean say two things no agree or fit together. The witness talk no match wetin dey ground as evidence.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The sudden noise in the examination hall caused a MOMENTARY distraction.
questions.e: The word 'momentary' means lasting for a very short time or brief. The distraction did not last long.
questions.p: 'Momentary' mean say something just happen for small time. The noise disrupt them for only brief moment.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
To prevent the spread of the disease, the veterinary officers had to CULL the infected chickens.
questions.e: In agriculture, to 'cull' means to select and slaughter animal population to prevent disease or control numbers.
questions.p: 'Cull' mean say make dem select sick animals kill make sickness no spread. So, to slaughter dem na the nearest meaning here.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The community leader spoke with great CANDOR about the security challenges facing the village.
questions.e: 'Candor' means the quality of being open, honest, and sincere in expression. He spoke with frankness about the issues.
questions.p: 'Candor' mean say person talk truth plain-plain without any corner-corner. The leader talk the security matter with clear frankness.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The principal's address was so EPHEMERAL that many students did not even realize the assembly had started before it ended.
questions.e: The word 'ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time or fleeting. 'Transient' is the closest synonym because it also refers to something that is temporary and passes quickly.
questions.p: 'Ephemeral' mean something wey no dey last at all, wey quickly pass. 'Transient' na the correct answer because e mean say something dey temporary or short-lived.

questions.q:
Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The minister's budget speech was filled with BOMBASTIC language that failed to address the real economic challenges facing the country.
questions.e: 'Bombastic' refers to speech or writing that is high-sounding, inflated, and pretentious but has little real meaning. 'Pompous' is the word nearest in meaning as it also describes language that is self-important and grandiloquent.
questions.p: 'Bombastic' speech na big grammar wey dey sound loud but no get beta meaning or substance. 'Pompous' na the word wey closest to am because e dey show say person dey make mouth or dey use high-sounding words to look important.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The principal warned the students that laziness will only PROVOKE failure in their examinations.
questions.e: 'Provoke' means to cause or bring about a reaction, usually negative. 'Avert' means to prevent or turn away an undesirable event, making it the exact opposite.
questions.p: 'Provoke' mean to cause something to happen, especially bad thing. But 'avert' mean to stop or prevent am before e happen, so na im be the opposite.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: Mr. Okoro bought a very GENUINE wristwatch at Computer Village in Ikeja.
questions.e: 'Genuine' means truly what something is said to be; authentic. Its direct antonym is 'fake', which means counterfeit or not real.
questions.p: 'Genuine' mean original thing wey no be copy. So the opposite na 'fake', wey mean say na counterfeit product.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The judge described the suspect's testimony as COGENT during the court session.
questions.e: 'Cogent' means clear, logical, and convincing. The exact opposite is 'weak', indicating an argument that lacks force or effectiveness.
questions.p: 'Cogent' mean strong point wey make sense well well. The opposite na 'weak' because the point no get power at all.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The new manager introduced radical reforms to AMELIORATE the working conditions of the staff.
questions.e: 'Ameliorate' means to make something bad or unsatisfactory better. 'Worsen' means to make something worse, which is the direct opposite.
questions.p: 'Ameliorate' mean to make something better pass before. So when you 'worsen' am, you don make the matter bad pass before.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The politician's ABJECT poverty before joining government surprised many villagers.
questions.e: 'Abject' describes something extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading, often used with poverty to mean extreme destitution. 'Affluent' means having a great deal of money, making it the correct antonym.
questions.p: 'Abject' poverty mean serious poverty where person dey suffer well well. The opposite na 'affluent', wey mean say person get plenty money and wealth.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: Chinedu showed remarkable BRAVERY when he confronted the armed robbers.
questions.e: 'Bravery' refers to courageous behavior or character. 'Cowardice' is lack of bravery, making it the direct opposite in meaning.
questions.p: 'Bravery' mean say person get mind to do strong thing. But 'cowardice' mean say person get fear and no get mind at all.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The novel was so TEDIOUS that most students slept off before chapter three.
questions.e: 'Tedious' means too long, slow, or dull; tiresome or monotonous. 'Exciting' is the direct opposite as it creates enthusiasm and interest.
questions.p: 'Tedious' mean book or work wey boring and dey sleep person. The opposite na 'exciting' because e dey sweet person to read or watch am.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The elders advised the youth to be DILIGENT in their daily business pursuits.
questions.e: 'Diligent' means having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties. 'Careless' implies a lack of attention or thoroughness, serving as its opposite.
questions.p: 'Diligent' mean person wey dey hardworking and serious with work. The opposite na 'careless' because the person dey do anyhow without concentration.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The community leader maintained a RELENTLESS campaign against cultism in the secondary school.
questions.e: 'Relentless' means ceaseless, constant, or unending. 'Intermittent' means occurring at irregular intervals or stopping and starting, which makes it the correct antonym.
questions.p: 'Relentless' mean something wey no dey stop at all. The opposite na 'intermittent' because e dey stop and start again.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The medical report declared that the patient was TRANSITORILY insane.
questions.e: 'Transitorily' means lasting for a short time; temporarily. The exact opposite is 'permanently', which means lasting or remaining unchanged indefinitely.
questions.p: 'Transitorily' mean something wey happen for small time only. So the opposite na 'permanently' because e go stay for long time or forever.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The path through the thick forest was so TORTUOUS that the travelers lost their way.
questions.e: 'Tortuous' means full of turns and twists, or extremely complex. 'Straight' means extending in a continuous direction without bends, making it the opposite.
questions.p: 'Tortuous' road mean road wey get plenty bend and curve up and down. The opposite na 'straight' road wey no get curve at all.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The football coach was EXASPERATED by the constant lateness of his key players.
questions.e: 'Exasperated' means intensely irritated or frustrated. 'Pleased' means feeling or showing pleasure and satisfaction, which is the direct opposite.
questions.p: 'Exasperated' mean say annoyance don hold person because of bad behavior. The opposite na 'pleased' because you happy with wetin person do.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: Their marriage union has remained HARMONIOUS despite external pressures.
questions.e: 'Harmonious' means free from disagreement or dissent; characterized by accord. 'Discordant' means disagreeing or incongruous, making it the appropriate antonym.
questions.p: 'Harmonious' mean people wey dey stay together peacefully without fight. The opposite na 'discordant' because na fight and disagreement full everywhere.

questions.q: Choose the option OPPOSITE in meaning to the word in capitals: The principal commended the student for his CANDID assessment of the school's facilities.
questions.e: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward; frank. 'Evasive' means tending to avoid commitment or self-revelation, especially by responding ambiguously, serving as the correct opposite.
questions.p: 'Candid' mean person wey dey talk true straight from heart without hiding anything. The opposite na 'evasive' because the person dey dodge question and hide truth.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The State Governor is expected to ________ the new ultra-modern market next Tuesday to allow traders to move in.
questions.e: To 'commission' a project or building means to formally open it for public use. Since the market is already built and traders are waiting to move in, 'commission' is the most appropriate vocabulary choice.
questions.p: 'Commission' na the correct word because e mean to formally open new project make people start to use am. Other options like 'construct' (to build) no fit because the market don ready already.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Due to the dusty harmattan winds, many children in the village have become highly ________ to respiratory infections.
questions.e: The word 'susceptible' means vulnerable or likely to be harmed by a particular thing. In this context, the dusty weather makes children easily catch infections.
questions.p: 'Susceptible' mean say person body weak to fight disease, so harmattan dust fit easily make the children sick. 'Immune' na the opposite, so na 'susceptible' be the correct answer.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The academic board found the student's excuse for missing the examination to be ________, as there was no medical report to back it up.
questions.e: 'Specious' means superficially plausible, but actually wrong or misleading. Without a medical report, the student's excuse appeared clever but was ultimately doubted and found to be false.
questions.p: 'Specious' mean say something look like true for face but na lie lie dey inside. Since the student no get medical report to show, the board see say the excuse na fake one.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Because of the high rate of inflation, the purchasing power of the local currency has continued to ________.
questions.e: 'Dwindle' means to gradually diminish in size, amount, or strength. High inflation reduces what money can buy, meaning purchasing power is decreasing.
questions.p: 'Dwindle' mean say something dey small small reduce. As things dey cost due to inflation, the power of money to buy things dey reduce, e no dey increase.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The school principal warned that any student caught cheating during the examination would be ________ from the institution.
questions.e: 'Expelled' is the correct educational term for officially forcing a student to leave a school permanently due to misconduct. 'Exiled' and 'deported' refer to countries, not schools.
questions.p: 'Expelled' na the correct word when dem pursue student comot for school permanently because of examination malpractice. 'Exiled' or 'deported' na for country matter.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The suspect was ________ of all charges by the high court due to a lack of concrete evidence linking him to the robbery.
questions.e: To be 'acquitted' means to be officially declared not guilty of a crime by a court. 'Pardoned' implies forgiveness after a conviction, which does not fit the context of lack of evidence.
questions.p: 'Acquitted' na the proper court word when judge say person free because evidence no dey to prove say he do the crime. 'Pardoned' mean say you do wrong but dem forgive you.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Chief Obi's ________ lifestyle made him popular among the villagers, as he always shared his wealth with the needy.
questions.e: 'Altruistic' means showing a disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others. Chief Obi's act of sharing his wealth with the needy is a sign of altruism.
questions.p: 'Altruistic' na person wey get clean heart, wey like to help people without expecting gain. Since Chief Obi dey share him wealth with the poor, na 'altruistic' fit am pass.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The bus driver was arrested because he failed to ________ his vehicle when the traffic light turned red.
questions.e: 'Halt' means to bring to a stop. Traffic laws require drivers to stop their vehicles when the traffic light is red.
questions.p: 'Halt' mean to stop. The driver get accident or police hold am because he no stop him motor when the traffic light show red.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The newspaper was sued for publishing a ________ article that damaged the reputation of the local businessman.
questions.e: A 'libellous' statement is a published false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation. This explains why the businessman sued the newspaper.
questions.p: 'Libellous' na when somebody write bad lie for newspaper or book to spoil another person name. Since the businessman sue dem, e mean say the article na bad lie.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The recent oil spill has severely ________ the aquatic life in the Niger Delta, leading to a massive loss of fish.
questions.e: 'Decimated' means to destroy a large proportion of something. The oil spill destroyed or killed a large number of fish, which fits the context.
questions.p: 'Decimated' mean say e destroy almost everything or kill plenty things. The oil spill spoil the water and kill plenty fish, so the fish population reduce well well.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The heavy downpour was so ________ that it flooded major streets in Lagos within an hour.
questions.e: 'Torrential' rain refers to rapidly flowing, exceptionally heavy rain. This is the type of rain that can cause rapid flooding in city streets.
questions.p: 'Torrential' rain na heavy rain wey dey fall with power. Na only that kind heavy rain fit flood Lagos streets inside just one hour.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Despite the provocative insults from the opposition party, the politician maintained his ________ and refused to respond angrily.
questions.e: 'Equanimity' means mental calmness, composure, and evenness of temper, especially in a difficult situation. The politician kept his cool despite being insulted.
questions.p: 'Equanimity' na when person keep him head cool and stay calm even when people dey do things to make am vex. The politician no vex, so he get equanimity.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
After a long and heated debate, the Senate committee decided to _______ the controversial bill indefinitely due to public outcry.
questions.e: "Shelve" is the correct term here because it means to postpone or set aside a plan or piece of legislation temporarily or indefinitely. "Veto" is incorrect because only the President (or executive head) can veto a bill, not a legislative committee. "Prorogue" means to discontinue a legislative session without dissolving parliament, while "quash" is a judicial term meaning to reject or void a legal decision.
questions.p: "Shelve" na the correct word because e mean to put plan or bill for side first. "Veto" no correct because na only President fit veto bill, no be committee. "Prorogue" na to close parliament session for some time, and "quash" na wetin court dey do to cancel case or judgment.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The governor's speech was filled with _______ remarks that did little to address the actual grievances of the striking civil servants.
questions.e: "Platitudinous" means filled with dull, flat, or overused remarks (platitudes) that lack original thought. This fits the context perfectly because empty, cliché remarks would not address the real issues of the striking workers. "Trenchant" means sharp and effective, "poignant" means deeply moving, and "pugnacious" means combative or eager to fight.
questions.p: "Platitudinous" na the correct word because e mean speech wey full of empty promises or common words wey no get deep meaning. This kind speech no fit solve the real wahala wey make the workers strike. "Trenchant" mean say speech make sense and get power, "poignant" na speech wey dey touch heart, and "pugnacious" na fight-fight speech, so dem no fit the sentence.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Either the class captain or the teachers _______ expected to present the report tomorrow.
questions.e: When 'either... or' connects two subjects, the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Since 'teachers' is plural and the event is in the future ('tomorrow'), the plural verb 'are' is correct.
questions.p: When 'either... or' join two subjects, the verb go follow the one wey close pass am. Since 'teachers' plenty and the thing never happen, na 'are' we go use.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Many a student _______ failed to realize the importance of consistent study until it is too late.
questions.e: The expression 'many a' is always followed by a singular countable noun and a singular verb. Therefore, 'has' is the correct verb to agree with 'Many a student'.
questions.p: This phrase 'many a' dey always carry singular noun and singular verb. So, na 'has' we suppose use, no be 'have'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The Vice-Chancellor, together with his principal officers, _______ attending the national summit in Abuja.
questions.e: When a subject is joined with other nouns using parenthetical expressions like 'together with', the verb agrees with the first subject. Here, 'The Vice-Chancellor' is singular, so the singular verb 'is' is correct.
questions.p: If you use 'together with' join two things, na the first one wey start the sentence dey control the verb. Since 'The Vice-Chancellor' na just one person, we must to use 'is'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The news about the petrol subsidy removal _______ causing a lot of anxiety across the country.
questions.e: The noun 'news' looks plural because it ends in 's', but it is uncountable and always takes a singular verb. Therefore, 'is' is the correct choice.
questions.p: Even though 'news' end with 's', na singular word wey no fit count. So, e must to carry singular verb like 'is'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The panel recommended that the suspended local government chairman _______ reinstated immediately.
questions.e: After verbs of recommending, demanding, or suggesting, the subjunctive mood is used. The subjunctive form for the verb 'to be' is 'be' for all subjects.
questions.p: When sentence dey talk about recommendation or command, we dey use subjunctive mood. The correct form na 'be', no matter who dem dey talk about for the sentence.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Two-thirds of the bags of rice _______ already been distributed to the internally displaced persons.
questions.e: When a fraction or percentage is used, the verb agrees with the noun in the 'of' phrase. Since 'bags' is plural, we use the plural verb 'have'.
questions.p: If you dey use fraction like 'two-thirds', the verb go follow the noun wey dey inside the 'of' part. Since 'bags of rice' plenty, we must use 'have'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
More than one candidate _______ protested the outcome of the post-UTME screening exercise.
questions.e: Despite the plural meaning, the construction 'more than one' grammatically takes a singular noun and a singular verb. Thus, 'has' is correct.
questions.p: Even though 'more than one' dey mean pass one person, the grammar rule talk say make we use singular verb. Na why 'has' correct here.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Everyone in the main auditorium _______ expected to stand up when the national anthem is being played.
questions.e: Indefinite pronouns like 'everyone', 'everybody', and 'someone' are singular and must take singular verbs. Therefore, 'is' is the correct verb.
questions.p: Words like 'everyone' or 'each person' na singular for grammar. So, e must to carry singular verb 'is' for this sentence.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Fifty thousand naira _______ too much to pay for a transport fare from Lagos to Ibadan.
questions.e: Expressed sums of money, periods of time, and distances are treated as single units of measurement and therefore take singular verbs. Thus, 'is' is correct.
questions.p: When we dey talk about total amount of money, distance, or time, we dey treat am as one block. Na why 'is' dey correct here instead of 'are'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
I, who _______ the class representative, should make the final decision on the excursion venue.
questions.e: A relative pronoun (who, which, that) takes a verb that agrees in person and number with its antecedent. The antecedent of 'who' is 'I', which requires the verb 'am'.
questions.p: The word 'who' dey represent the person wey start the talk, wey be 'I'. Since 'I' dey always carry 'am', the correct answer na 'am'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The school committee _______ decided to postpone the inter-house sports competition till next term.
questions.e: Collective nouns like 'committee' take a singular verb when the group acts as a single, unified unit. Here, they made a single joint decision, so 'has' is correct.
questions.p: When committee dey do something as one group, we dey treat dem as single body. So, na singular verb 'has' we go use for here.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Not only the students but also their teacher _______ invited to the governor's banquet last night.
questions.e: When 'not only... but also' is used, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Their teacher' is singular, and the past tense 'last night' makes 'was' the correct choice.
questions.p: For 'not only... but also', the verb must follow the subject wey close to am pass. Since 'their teacher' na one person, and e happen for past, na 'was' we go pick.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The Principal, together with his vice-principals and the senior prefect, ________ expected to address the assembly this morning.
questions.e: In English concord, when a singular subject is joined to other nouns using parenthetical expressions like 'together with', 'as well as', or 'along with', the verb remains singular. The true subject is 'The Principal', which is singular, so it requires the singular verb 'is'.
questions.p: When singular subject follow join body with 'together with', the verb go still dey singular because those extra words no dey change the subject to plural. Na why 'The Principal' (singular) must carry 'is' for this sentence.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Amina is one of the few students who ________ consistently scored straight A's in the mock examinations.
questions.e: In the structure 'one of the [plural noun] who', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural noun 'students' (the antecedent), not 'one'. Consequently, the verb must be plural ('have') to agree with 'students'.
questions.p: For this structure 'one of the students who', the 'who' dey point to the 'students' wey plenty, no be just 'one' person. Na why the verb must be plural ('have') to match the plenty students.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
By the time the principal arrived at the assembly ground, the prefects _______ the latecomers.
questions.e: The sentence describes an action (punishing latecomers) that was completed before another action in the past (the principal's arrival). The past perfect tense ('had punished') is the correct verb form for the earlier past action.
questions.p: This sentence dey talk about action (to punish latecomers) where happen and finish before another past action (when principal reach school). Na why we use past perfect tense 'had punished' for wetin happen first.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The wet clothes have _______ on the line since yesterday morning.
questions.e: The verb 'hang' has two past participle forms: 'hung' (to suspend an object) and 'hanged' (to execute someone). Since we are referring to wet clothes, the correct past participle is 'hung'.
questions.p: The verb 'hang' get two past participle: 'hung' (to hang cloth or bag) and 'hanged' (to hang person die). Since na wet clothes we dey talk about, 'hung' na the correct word to use.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The disciplinary committee insisted that Obi _______ the school rules without further delay.
questions.e: The verb 'insist' triggers the subjunctive mood in the noun clause that follows. In the subjunctive mood, we use the base form of the verb ('obey'), regardless of whether the subject ('Obi') is singular.
questions.p: Because of the word 'insisted', the sentence dey use subjunctive mood. For this style, we must use the base form of the verb 'obey', even though 'Obi' na singular person.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
If Chinedu had studied harder for the post-UTME, he _______ admission into the university last year.
questions.e: This is a third conditional sentence, which refers to an impossible past condition and its probable past result. The correct structure is 'if + past perfect (had studied)... would have + past participle (would have secured)'.
questions.p: This one na third conditional sentence where dey talk about wetin for happen for past if condition been change. The correct pattern na 'if + had studied... would have secured'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
It is high time we _______ our preparation for the upcoming examinations.
questions.e: The construction 'It is high time' is followed by a subject and a verb in the simple past tense (past subjunctive) to indicate that something should have been done already. Therefore, 'started' is the correct option.
questions.p: Anytime you see 'It is high time' followed by person or people, the next verb must dey simple past. Na why 'started' correct here, even though we dey talk about wetin we suppose do now.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Mrs. Adeleke _______ in this secondary school for over fifteen years before she was promoted to vice-principal.
questions.e: The past perfect continuous tense ('had been teaching') is used to show that an action started in the past and continued up until another time in the past (before her promotion).
questions.p: We use past perfect continuous tense 'had been teaching' because Mrs. Adeleke dey do the teaching work continuously before another past action (her promotion) take happen.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
No sooner had the invigilator distributed the question papers than the bell _______.
questions.e: In sentences starting with limiting adverbs like 'No sooner', the structure is 'No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than + subject + simple past'. Therefore, 'rang' is the correct past simple verb.
questions.p: When sentence start with 'No sooner', the rule na 'No sooner had... than + simple past'. Na why 'rang' na the correct option to complete the sentence.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Currently, the new classroom block _______ to the school board.
questions.e: 'Belongs' is a stative verb representing state or possession. Stative verbs are not typically used in continuous tenses (like 'is belonging'), even when referring to a current state.
questions.p: The word 'belong' na stative verb where dey show possession. We no dey use '-ing' with am, so 'is belonging' wrong. Na 'belongs' be the correct one.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
I would rather you _______ the money to the bank yesterday as I instructed.
questions.e: When 'would rather' is followed by a subject and refers to a past time (indicated by 'yesterday'), the past perfect tense ('had paid') must be used to express a past preference or regret.
questions.p: Because 'would rather' get subject after am and we dey talk about past time (yesterday), we must use past perfect tense 'had paid'. This one dey show wetin we wish say happen for past.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Every morning, before the bell rings, the janitor _______ the classrooms.
questions.e: The phrase 'Every morning' indicates a habitual action. Simple present tense ('sweeps') is used to describe regular habits or routines.
questions.p: The words 'Every morning' show say the action na habit where dey happen every day. Na why we use simple present tense 'sweeps' for there.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
By this time next month, my elder sister _______ from the University of Ibadan.
questions.e: The phrase 'By this time next month' indicates a specific deadline in the future. The future perfect tense ('will have graduated') is used to show that an action will be completed before this specific future time.
questions.p: Since we get 'By this time next month', e mean say the action go finish before that future time reach. Na why we use future perfect tense 'will have graduated'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Yesterday afternoon, the tired student _______ on the bench under the mango tree to rest.
questions.e: The verb 'lie' (meaning to recline or rest horizontally) has 'lay' as its simple past tense. 'Laid' is the past tense of 'lay' (to place something down), which requires a direct object. Since the student rested on the bench, 'lay' is correct.
questions.p: The word 'lie' (to lie down) get 'lay' as its past tense. 'Laid' na the past tense of 'lay' (to put object down). Since the student lie down to rest, 'lay' na the correct past tense.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
If Obi ________ harder last term, he would have passed the UTME with a score above 300.
questions.e: This sentence uses the third conditional to express an imaginary situation in the past and its past consequence. The structure requires the past perfect tense ('had studied') in the 'if-clause' to match 'would have passed' in the main clause.
questions.p: Dis sentence dey talk about something wey for happen for past but e no happen (third conditional). Since the main part get 'would have passed', the 'if' part must use past perfect tense, which be 'had studied'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The principal insisted that every student ________ present at the assembly ground before 7:30 a.m.
questions.e: The verb 'insisted' triggers the mandative subjunctive mood in the 'that-clause'. In the subjunctive mood, the base form of the verb ('be') is used for all subjects, regardless of whether they are singular or plural.
questions.p: Because the word 'insisted' dey show command or strong demand, we must use the subjunctive mood. For subjunctive mood, the verb no dey change to 'is' or 'was'; e must remain for the original base form wey be 'be'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Amina was advised to apply ___ a scholarship before the closing date expires next Friday.
questions.e: We use the preposition 'for' when making a formal request or application for something like a job, scholarship, or visa. 'Apply to' is used when writing to an institution or person directly.
questions.p: When you dey find scholarship or job, na 'apply for' you go use. E show say na the scholarship she dey find.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The noisy market women refused to comply ___ the directives given by the local government chairman.
questions.e: The verb 'comply' is standardly followed by the preposition 'with' when obeying rules, regulations, or directives. No other preposition collocates correctly with 'comply' in this context.
questions.p: Standard grammar rule na 'comply with' rules or directives. E mean say make person obey wetong authority talk.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The football match was called ___ due to the heavy downpour that flooded the Onikan stadium.
questions.e: The phrasal verb 'call off' means to cancel an event or arrangement. Since the heavy rain disrupted the game, it was cancelled.
questions.p: When rain spoil match or dem cancel event, na 'call off' dem dey use am. E mean say the match no happen again.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Chidi takes ___ his elder brother in his gentle manner of speaking and walking.
questions.e: The phrasal verb 'take after' means to resemble a parent or older relative in appearance or character. Chidi resembles his elder brother.
questions.p: If person resemble im senior brother or papa for character or face, we dey talk say im 'take after' am.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The fire service personnel managed to put ___ the inferno before it razed the entire plaza.
questions.e: To 'put out' is a phrasal verb that means to extinguish a fire or light. 'Put off' means to postpone, making 'out' the only correct choice here.
questions.p: Na 'put out' dem dey use for fire when dem wan quench am. E different from 'put off' wey mean postponement.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The corrupt politician tried to gloss ___ his financial scandals during the televised interview.
questions.e: To 'gloss over' something means to treat it cursorily, try to conceal it, or avoid dealing with its unpleasant details. This fits the politician's attempt to hide his scandals.
questions.p: To 'gloss over' matter mean say you wan cover am up or make people no notice the bad thing wey you do. Na im the politician try do.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The angry mob insisted that the suspected thief must account ___ every kobo stolen from the shop.
questions.e: The phrasal verb 'account for' means to explain, give a reckoning of, or take responsibility for something. The thief must explain what happened to the stolen money.
questions.p: If dem ask you make you explain wetong happen to money or property, na 'account for' you go use. E mean say you must talk true.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The old woman's health deteriorated rapidly because she was deprived ___ basic medical care.
questions.e: The verb 'deprive' is grammatically followed by the preposition 'of' when indicating what someone is kept from having. Saying 'deprived from' is a common Nigerian English error.
questions.p: No be 'deprived from' o! Correct grammar na 'deprived of'. E mean say dem deny person something wey suppose belong to am.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
When Uncle Chiadi bought a brand new luxury car, he thought it would solve his transportation problems, but it turned out to be a 'white elephant'. This means that the car was...
o: a symbol of immense wealth and prestige
a very expensive but useless possession
a vehicle that frequently gets involved in accidents
questions.e: The idiom 'white elephant' is used to describe a possession that is extremely costly to maintain but yields little to no practical use or value. In this context, the luxury car brought more trouble and expense than actual utility.
questions.p: White elephant mean say something cost well-well to buy or maintain, but e no get any useful work wey e dey do for the person.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
Amina decided to 'burn the midnight oil' in order to pass the upcoming UTME with an outstanding score.
o: study or work late into the night
pray fervently for success in the dark
waste her kerosene during the night
wake up early to cook for her family
questions.e: To 'burn the midnight oil' means to read, study, or work late into the night. Amina was staying up late to prepare for her examination.
questions.p: To 'burn the midnight oil' mean say make person stay awake read book or work late for night so that eye go open.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
The partners in the boutique business at Balogun Market no longer 'see eye to eye' on financial matters.
o: look at each other's eyes during meetings
trust each other with physical cash
questions.e: The idiom 'to see eye to eye' means to share the same position, opinion, or agreement on an issue. Since the partners no longer see eye to eye, it means they disagree on financial matters.
questions.p: When people 'see eye to eye', e mean say dem dey agree on top the same matter. For here, the partners no dey agree again.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
Chinedu was advised not to 'throw caution to the wind' during his campaign for the post of Senior Prefect.
o: act in a completely reckless or careless manner
speak arrogantly to the junior students
fail to consult the school authorities
waste his campaign funds on unnecessary items
questions.e: To 'throw caution to the wind' means to act in an extremely reckless, carefree, or risky manner without considering the consequences. Chinedu was warned to remain careful and responsible during his campaigns.
questions.p: To 'throw caution to the wind' mean say make person do things anyhow without to care about the bad tin wey fit happen after.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
After years of silent rivalry, the two brothers finally decided to 'bury the hatchet' during the New Year festival.
o: hold a grand feast to show off their wealth
settle their differences and make peace
buy new farming implements for their father
hide their weapons to avoid police arrest
questions.e: The expression 'bury the hatchet' means to end a quarrel, conflict, or long-standing rivalry and reconcile with one another. The brothers chose to make peace during the festival.
questions.p: To 'bury the hatchet' mean say make people stop fight, forget past vex, and make peace with each other.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
The politician's promise to build a world-class stadium in our local government area turned out to be a 'pie in the sky'.
o: a highly successful and celebrated project
an expensive project funded by foreign loans
a secret plan kept away from the public
an empty promise that is unlikely to be realized
questions.e: A 'pie in the sky' refers to an idea, plan, or promise that is pleasing to contemplate but is highly unrealistic and unlikely to ever happen or be achieved.
questions.p: Pie in the sky mean say plan or promise wey sweet for ear but dem know say e no go fit happen for real life.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
Efe let the 'cat out of the bag' when he accidentally revealed the surprise birthday plans for his mother.
o: revealed a secret carelessly or by accident
lost a valuable pet in the market
lied to protect his siblings from punishment
made an unforgivable mistake in public
questions.e: To 'let the cat out of the bag' is a common idiom that means to disclose a secret, often accidentally or prematurely.
questions.p: To 'let the cat out of the bag' mean say person talk secret out by mistake make people know wetin dem suppose hide.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
With the current high cost of living, many civil servants find it difficult to 'make ends meet'.
o: travel to their hometowns for holidays
earn enough money to cover basic expenses
pay off all their outstanding bank loans
questions.e: To 'make ends meet' means to earn just enough money to live on or to cover essential monthly expenditures like food, rent, and bills.
questions.p: 'Make ends meet' mean say make person get reach money wey go fit buy food, pay rent, and do other basic things wey life need.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
The underdog team from Enugu really 'stole a march on' the defending champions in the first half of the tournament.
o: bribed the match officials to favor them
played a very rough and aggressive game
used defensive tactics to delay the game
gained an unexpected advantage over them by acting early
questions.e: To 'steal a march on' someone means to gain an unexpected or sneaky advantage over them, especially by acting ahead of them or before they realize what is happening.
questions.p: To 'steal a march on' person mean say you smart pass dem or get advantage over dem because you move fast do wetin dem no expect.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
Tunde could not attend the class reunion because he was feeling 'under the weather'.
o: trapped in heavy rain on his way
busy working on his farm in the village
angry with the organizers of the event
questions.e: The idiom 'under the weather' means to feel slightly sick, ill, tired, or indisposed.
questions.p: When person dey 'under the weather', e mean say the person body no too set, or say e dey sick small.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
The manager decided to 'skate on thin ice' by using the company's emergency savings for the speculative investment.
o: seek financial advice from unreliable sources
show off his authority over the subordinates
save the company from imminent bankruptcy
take a highly risky or dangerous course of action
questions.e: To 'skate on thin ice' means to take a huge risk, be in a precarious situation, or do something that could easily lead to trouble or disaster.
questions.p: To 'skate on thin ice' mean say make person do something wey risky well-well, wey fit make am fall enter big trouble if e go wrong.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
Instead of addressing the main issue of corruption in the department, the speaker chose to 'beat about the bush'.
o: clear the weeds around the secretariat
accuse the wrong group of people
avoid talking about the main topic directly
speak with absolute confidence and clarity
questions.e: To 'beat about the bush' (or beat around the bush) means to discuss a matter without coming directly to the point, often to avoid talking about an uncomfortable topic.
questions.p: 'Beat about the bush' mean say make person dey talk plenty other things instead of to hit the main point wey dey ground.

questions.q: Chidi was strongly warned by his father not to pay for the second-hand car before inspecting it, so that he would not buy a pig in a poke. What is the meaning of the italicized expression?
o: purchase something without seeing or assessing it beforehand.
pay too much money for an item of low quality.
engage in an illegal business transaction.
acquire an asset that brings nothing but bad luck.
questions.e: The idiom 'to buy a pig in a poke' means to purchase something without examining it first, which often leads to disappointment. Chidi's father wanted him to inspect the car to ensure he knew its actual condition before paying. Therefore, option A is the correct interpretation.
questions.p: Dis idiom 'to buy a pig in a poke' mean make person pay for wetin he never see or check well. Chidi papa dey warn am make he check the motor first, so dat he no go buy wetin go come pain am later. Correct option na A.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes.
As soon as the vigilant security guard raised the alarm, the suspected thief showed a clean pair of heels. This means that the suspect...
o: ran away very quickly to escape.
tried to bribe the security guard.
questions.e: The idiomatic expression 'showed a clean pair of heels' means to run away very fast, especially to escape capture. In this context, the suspect fled immediately upon hearing the alarm. This makes option B the correct answer.
questions.p: To 'show a clean pair of heels' mean say person run escape sharp-sharp make dem no catch am. As the security guard raise alarm, the suspect just japa (run away) very fast. Na why B be the correct answer.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'Had the bus not broken down at Ore, we would have caught the first flight out of Lagos.'
o: We did not travel by bus, so we caught the first flight easily.
We missed the flight because the bus broke down at Ore.
The flight was cancelled, which caused the bus to break down at Ore.
The bus broke down at Ore, but we still managed to catch the flight.
questions.e: The sentence uses a third conditional structure to show a hypothetical past regret. Because the bus broke down, the negative outcome of missing the flight occurred.
questions.p: Na because moto break down for Ore make us miss dat flight. Dat sentence dey show say wetin we no expect happen, so we no reach airport on time.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'Chinedu’s promotion was nothing to write home about.'
o: His promotion was modest or underwhelming, not warranting much excitement.
His promotion was extremely impressive and deserved loud celebrations.
His promotion was so disappointing that nobody bothered to talk about it.
His promotion happened so far away from home that his family did not know.
questions.e: The idiom 'nothing to write home about' means something is ordinary, mediocre, or not particularly exciting. Therefore, Chinedu's promotion was not very impressive.
questions.p: Dat idiom mean say wetin happen no too sweet like dat. E ordinary gidigba, so no need make person start to pop champagne or jubilation up and down.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'Hardly had Emeka stepped into the hall when the lights went off.'
o: Emeka intentionally turned off the lights as soon as he entered the hall.
The lights went off a long time before Emeka arrived at the hall.
The lights went off immediately after Emeka entered the hall.
Emeka refused to enter the hall because the lights were already off.
questions.e: The correlative structure 'Hardly had... when...' indicates that two actions happened in quick succession, with the second event (lights going off) following immediately after the first.
questions.p: As Emeka just enter hall, NEPA take light sharp sharp. E show say two things happen back to back without waste of time.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'If Zainab were less obstinate, she would listen to her parents' advice.'
o: Zainab will soon start listening to her parents if they advise her better.
Zainab is stubborn, so she does not take her parents' advice.
Zainab listens to her parents because she is very obedient.
Zainab used to be stubborn, but now she listens to her parents.
questions.e: The subjunctive conditional 'If Zainab were less obstinate' implies she is currently stubborn ('obstinate'). Consequently, she fails to heed her parents' counsel.
questions.p: Zainab stubborn like person wey demur, na dat one make she no dey hear word from her papa and mama. Dis na present situation o.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'The principal’s warning fell on deaf ears.'
o: The students completely ignored or disregarded the principal's warning.
The students had hearing impairments and could not hear the principal.
The principal spoke too softly for anyone in the assembly to understand.
The principal whispered the warning so nobody else could listen.
questions.e: The idiom 'fall on deaf ears' means that advice or warnings are ignored, disregarded, or unheeded by the listeners.
questions.p: Principal warn dem tire, but dem carry am play for head. E mean say dem no gree take correction at all at all.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'Mrs. Okoro speaks English with a heavy Igbo accent, and so does her sister.'
o: Both Mrs. Okoro and her sister speak English with an Igbo accent.
Only Mrs. Okoro speaks English, while her sister speaks Igbo fluently.
Mrs. Okoro speaks with an Igbo accent, but her sister speaks differently.
Neither Mrs. Okoro nor her sister can speak proper English.
questions.e: The phrase 'and so does her sister' is an affirmative agreement structure showing that the sister shares the exact same linguistic trait as Mrs. Okoro.
questions.p: Na both of them get that same Igbo flavor for mouth when dem dey speak English. Wetin Mrs. Okoro dey do, na im sister too dey do.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'The politician’s promise turned out to be a mere flash in the pan.'
o: The promise created a huge scandal that led to his resignation.
The politician successfully fulfilled all his campaign promises quickly.
The promise was a brilliant idea that brought lasting development.
The promise was temporary, spectacular at first, but failed quickly.
questions.e: A 'flash in the pan' refers to something that promises great success initially but quickly fails or proves to be short-lived and ineffective.
questions.p: That promise na just mouth action wey sweet for beginning, but e no last. E fade away like smoke immediately.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'However hard Aminu tried, he could not solve the mathematics puzzle.'
o: Despite his best efforts, Aminu failed to find the solution to the puzzle.
Aminu gave up immediately without trying to solve the puzzle.
Aminu solved the puzzle easily because he tried very hard.
Aminu only solved the puzzle after trying several difficult methods.
questions.e: The concessive clause 'However hard Aminu tried' indicates maximum effort, followed by a contrastive failure ('could not solve').
questions.p: Even though Aminu use all im brain and try tire, maths puzzle pass am. E no fit solve am at all.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'It never rains but it pours in that family.'
o: Members of that family argue frequently whenever it starts to rain.
The family’s house always gets flooded during the rainy season.
That family is extremely wealthy and showers money on visitors.
Misfortunes or troubles always happen in series, not singly, for that family.
questions.e: The proverb 'It never rains but it pours' means that when bad things happen, they tend to happen all at once or in large quantities.
questions.p: For dat family, once problem start to come, e dey jam body like trailer. Trouble no dey come one by one.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'Bala would rather trek to the market than board a commercial motorcycle.'
o: Bala rides a motorcycle to the market and walks back home.
Bala prefers walking to the market over riding on a commercial motorcycle.
Bala dislikes trekking, but he has no money for a commercial motorcycle.
Bala always takes a commercial motorcycle because trekking is too stressful.
questions.e: The structure 'would rather X than Y' expresses a strong personal preference for option X over option Y.
questions.p: Bala like to use him leg waka go market pass make e join okada. Na him personal choice be dat.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'The manager let the cat out of the bag regarding the new salary scale.'
o: The manager intentionally hid the salary files from the workers.
The manager caught a stray cat hiding inside his office bag.
The manager accidentally or prematurely revealed the secret salary scale.
The manager dismissed the workers who leaked the salary information.
questions.e: The idiom 'let the cat out of the bag' means to reveal a secret, often unintentionally or prematurely.
questions.p: Manager talk wetin suppose be secret about salary. E open mouth talk am out before time.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'No sooner had the teacher entered the class than the students became quiet.'
o: The teacher waited for the students to become quiet before entering.
The students kept making noise even after the teacher entered the class.
The students were already quiet before the teacher entered the classroom.
The students became silent immediately the teacher stepped into the classroom.
questions.e: The correlative structure 'No sooner had... than...' denotes immediate succession, meaning the silence followed the teacher's entry instantly.
questions.p: As teacher just step leg enter class, everywhere come quiet straight. No wasting time at all.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'Tolu is burning the candle at both ends to meet the project deadline.'
o: Tolu is overworking himself and exhausting his energy to finish the project.
Tolu is wasting resources by lighting candles unnecessarily during the day.
Tolu is enjoying his work because the project deadline is still far away.
Tolu is working only during the night and sleeping throughout the day.
questions.e: The idiom 'burning the candle at both ends' means overworking oneself by maintaining an exhausting schedule, leading to fatigue.
questions.p: Tolu dey stress himself too much, working day and night just to finish dat project. E dey drain him energy scatter.

questions.q: Choose the option that best explains the sentence: 'Had I known about the traffic gridlock on the bridge, I would have taken the alternative route.'
o: There was no traffic on the bridge, so I reached my destination early.
I did not know about the traffic, so I got stuck because I used the bridge.
I avoided the bridge because someone warned me about the traffic.
I knew about the traffic, so I successfully used an alternative route.
questions.e: This inverted third conditional sentence expresses past regret; the speaker implies ignorance of the traffic situation led to taking the congested bridge.
questions.p: If to say I know say jam dey for bridge, I for pass another road. But because I no know, na im make I enter trap.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Neither of the two prefects completed _____ assignment before the assembly.
questions.e: The phrase 'Neither of' is singular, so it requires the singular masculine or gender-neutral pronoun 'his' in traditional grammar. Option B correctly matches the singular subject.
questions.p: 'Neither of' dey singular, so na 'his' you go use. Option B correct well well.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The principal gave the award to Chinedu and _____.
questions.e: The pronoun follows the preposition 'to', requiring the objective case 'me'. 'Chinedu and me' is the object of the verb gave.
questions.p: As the word 'to' dey front, na object pronoun 'me' you suppose put. Option B na him be am.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Let you and _____ handle this difficult Physics practical.
questions.e: Following the imperative verb 'Let', the objective case is required for pronouns. 'Let me' means 'me' is correct.
questions.p: After 'Let', make you use objective pronoun like 'me'. Option B correct.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Emeka is one of those students who always submit _____ homework early.
questions.e: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'students', which is plural. Therefore, the possessive pronoun must also be plural 'their'.
questions.p: Na 'students' the word 'who' dey talk about, and plural e be. Na 'their' fit follow am.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
The committee presented _____ report to the governor yesterday.
questions.e: A collective noun acting as a single unit takes a singular pronoun. 'Its' correctly refers to the committee as one body.
questions.p: Committee dey act as one body here, so na singular pronoun 'its' you go use.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Gbenga and Ngozi respect _____ during their debates.
questions.e: 'Each other' is used when referring to exactly two people. Since Gbenga and Ngozi are two, option B is correct.
questions.p: Because na two people dey inside, na 'each other' you go use. Option B na the correct answer.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Nobody knows the secret except _____.
questions.e: The word 'except' acts as a preposition here, requiring objective case pronouns. Therefore, 'her and me' is the correct choice.
questions.p: Presiposition 'except' dey demand objective pronouns like 'her and me'. Option B correct.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
You locked the laboratory door, _____?
questions.e: The main verb 'locked' is in the simple past tense and affirmative. The question tag must use the auxiliary 'did' in the negative: 'didn't you'.
questions.p: As 'locked' dey past tense, na 'didn't you' be the correct question tag.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Aminu rarely misses morning devotion, _____?
questions.e: The word 'rarely' makes the sentence negative in meaning. A negative statement requires a positive question tag ('does he').
questions.p: Word like 'rarely' make the sentence negative, so the tag must positive. Na 'does he'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Let us go to the market now, _____?
questions.e: Suggestions starting with 'Let us' or 'Let's' always take the question tag 'shall we'. This is a standard grammatical rule.
questions.p: Anytime sentence start with 'Let us', the correct question tag na 'shall we'.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Open the gates for the principal's car, _____?
questions.e: Imperative sentences (commands or requests) usually take 'will you' or 'won't you' as their question tag. Option A is standard.
questions.p: If person give command like this, na 'will you' you go use for back.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
I am taller than _____ in this athletics team.
questions.e: In formal comparisons using 'than', the pronoun completes the implied clause ('than he is tall'). Thus, the subjective pronoun 'he' is correct.
questions.p: For formal grammar, after 'than', na subjective pronoun 'he' you suppose put.

questions.q:
Choose the option that best completes the gap.
Everybody in the hall stood up when the anthem was played, _____?
questions.e: Indefinite pronouns like 'everybody' take the plural pronoun 'they' in question tags. The verb 'stood' requires 'didn't they'.
questions.p: Word like 'everybody' dey take 'they' for question tag, and 'stood' mean say 'didn't' must join am.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The principal was impressed by the ______ performance of the JSS3 students during the inter-house sports.
questions.e: When stacking multiple adjectives before a noun, opinion adjectives ('brilliant') generally come before classifying/material adjectives ('athletic'). Therefore, 'brilliant athletic' follows the correct English word order rule.
questions.p: When you wan arrange two adjectives before noun, opinion word like 'brilliant' dey come first before classification word like 'athletic'. Na why 'brilliant athletic' correct.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Chinedu walked ______ into the examination hall because he was well prepared for the test.
questions.e: An adverb is required to modify the verb 'walked'. 'Confidently' is the correct adverb of manner that shows how he walked into the hall.
questions.p: Na adverb we need here to tell us how the boy walk. 'Confidently' na the right adverb of manner wey show as e enter the hall.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Mama Tobi sold her ______ car to buy a brand new bus for her transport business.
questions.e: The Royal Order of Adjectives places age before color, and color before origin/noun adjunct. 'Old' (age) comes before 'brown' (color), making 'old brown Toyota' the correct choice.
questions.p: As protocol follow for adjectives, age ('old') must come before colour ('brown'). Na why 'old brown Toyota' correct pass.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The tired farmer worked ______ throughout the hot afternoon to clear the yam ridge.
